n_question: Serious. The printed Table 2 header gives N = 62 ($4) / 60 ($8) for every row; the critics instead used per-row Ns inferred from Article 2's regression models (41/26 for middle-piece rows, 47/38 for last-piece rows). At the printed header n, 6.16 (N = 62) and both 7.97 cells (N = 60) are GRIM-CONSISTENT, so those three labels hold only under the critics' cross-article inference. The 2017 erratum and the data release show every row had its own n (Table 1: 64-70; Table 2: 39-63 at $4, 29-61 at $8), usually LARGER than printed; at those true ns the flagged means become consistent, except the two gender percentages whose printed values themselves were later changed (to 60.0 and 51.5). So the GRIM failures are real inconsistencies with the printed n, caused mainly by misreported n (plus one duplicated row).
cells_not_itemised: None: the Appendix itemises every granularity error. Age, height and weight were deliberately excluded from GRIM testing by the critics.
notes: Itemised cells copied from the Appendix of the BMC Nutrition article (read via Europe PMC full-text XML, PMC7050813); mean strings cross-checked against the critics' own copy-pasted transcription (github.com/OmnesRes/pizzapizza, Python/paper1_table1.txt and paper1_table2.txt) and the 'Original Table' reproductions in 'Statistical infarction'.
